html:
SMTO-EXE-0120 — The file upload didn't finish

GUID: 21e892c4-29ef-5d7a-9a06-117c312e34c9
Slug: browser-upload-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO tried to add a file to a web page, but something went wrong. The page may already have received the file, so it might be attached already.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO: "Look at the page and tell me whether the file is already attached." Don't ask it to upload again yet. The page may have accepted the file before the error appeared.
  2. Don't let SMTO press Submit or Send on that form until you know which files are attached. Submitting now could send the wrong files or send the form twice.
  3. If the file is not attached, ask SMTO to upload it once more. Once you know it isn't there, uploading again won't create a duplicate.
  4. If it keeps failing, check the website accepts that file type and size. Some sites reject certain file types or large files during the upload.

What success looks like

  • The page shows the file attached exactly once, and the form has not been sent twice.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file name and website, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't submit the form repeatedly hoping one attempt works.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A browser upload_file operation on the Gateway raised an unexpected non-timeout error; effect_unknown records whether the file had already been handed to the page.

What this means

  • An upload operation raised a non-timeout exception outside the specific target/path checks; the service records whether the upload action was attempted. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • An upload operation raised a non-timeout exception outside the specific target/path checks; the service records whether the upload action was attempted.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original upload receipt, file input state and any external submission before repeating the action.

How to fix it

  • BrowserService._execute mapped an unclassified exception from upload_file (after the target and path checks) to upload_failed; provider text is withheld. Inspect browser.snapshot of the file input and page and the receipt's effect_unknown before retrying, and never resubmit the surrounding form until its state is confirmed.
  • Inspect the file input and page state before retrying; do not submit the form twice.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the file input and page state before retrying; do not submit the form twice.

How to verify the fix

  • The original file-selection/upload state is reconciled and a new action is performed only if still required.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
